newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's CPI up 1.2 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's CPI up 1.2 pct in June.

text.p: Colombia's consumer price index rose 1.2 percent in June, compared with a 1.14 percent rise in the same month last year, the National Statistics Department (DANE) said Wednesday.
As measured on a cumulative basis, CPI rose 11.26 percent in the first six months of the year, versus 14.04 percent in the first half of 1996, DANE said.
Inflation in 1996 was 21.63 percent, and the central bank has set an 18 percent target for this year.
The cumulative rise in CPI for the last 12 months is 18.67 percent, 1.03 percentage points lower than the cumulative 12-month figure to June 1996, DANE said.
It said the cumulative rise for the last 12 months is the lowest since the year ended June 1986.
The June rise in CPI was driven by a 2.62 percent increase in the cost of alcoholic beverages and tobacco, according to DANE. It said beer prices alone shot up 5.87 percent.
Housing costs increased 1.38 percent, while fuel and public services jumped 2.35 percent.
The 1.2 percent increase in June CPI compared to a 1.62 percent rise in May.
